properties.decision:
DECIDED by Anthony 2026-08-05: "I like and approve: a tool that describes the design at a given path — id, label, node counts, mint stamp — without binding to it. Your agent walks the tree (which it can, as you said); reflow2 says what's in each .reflow2 it finds. That splits cleanly along the no-file-I/O rule."

THE SHAPE. Two responsibilities, split along the line this project already draws. THE AGENT FINDS THE DIRECTORIES — walking a tree for `.reflow2` is file IO, which reflow2 does not do and does not need to, because the ambient agent does it well (`dec:agent-navigates-content`, and its parent `dec:three-party-checks`: "the LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides"). REFLOW2 SAYS WHAT IS IN ONE — given a path, it reports the design's identity: graph id, label, how many nodes of what kind, the stamp it was minted under. Neither half can do the other's job, and the split is the same one that already governs content navigation and coverage sweeps.

⭐ WHAT IT REPLACES, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS ASK WAS THE WRONG ONE. Anthony first asked for "a reflow2 tool to simply return all graph_ids". Measured before answering: that returns ONE PER STORE. Storage keys are `{graph_id}\x00{type}\x00{id}` and `dynograph_storage::keys::graph_prefix` exists, so the FOUNDATION supports many graphs per store — but reflow2 opens one graph per store by convention (`DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID`, one `.reflow2` per project), and the three graphs in the hxm_program field report are three separate STORES. Enumerating within a store is therefore a true answer to a question nobody has. Describing a store found on disk is the question that was actually being asked.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE. It settles the DISCOVERY half of `req:a-session-chooses-its-design` — how an agent learns what designs exist before anything is created, which is what would have prevented the accidental third graph (`dec:no-design-here-never-looked`). It does NOT settle how a session is then POINTED at the chosen design: editing `.mcp.json` and reconnecting, versus a graph reference carried per call, remains open at `dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design`, where Anthony has expressed a lean toward the first and the counter ([BL-123] — the `/mcp` reconnect is the one step an autonomous agent cannot take) is recorded against it.

⚠️ THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES THE BUILD, and it must not be discovered in the field: A ROCKSDB STORE HELD BY A RUNNING SERVER IS EXCLUSIVELY LOCKED. Describing a design at a path while another session holds it needs a shared or read-only open. `--shared` exists and this repo's own `.mcp.json` does not pass it — which is separately why the stale-server export replay is needed at every release cut. THE TOOL MUST SAY "BUSY" RATHER THAN FAILING OPAQUELY OR, WORSE, REPORTING NOTHING FOUND: a describe that answers "no design" because the store was locked would be the same defect this whole thread began with, in a new place.

AND THE RULE THIS SERVES, which survives whatever the pointing mechanism turns out to be: DEFAULT WHEN EXACTLY ONE DESIGN IS REACHABLE; REFUSE AND LIST THEM WHEN SEVERAL ARE. Discovery is what makes the second half of that sentence possible — you cannot list what you never looked for.

NOT CHECKED, and it decides whether this is a new tool or a parameter: whether `design_identity` could take an optional path and answer for a store it is not bound to.
properties.name: DECIDED — discovery is a pair: the agent walks the tree, and reflow2 describes the design at a path without binding to it
properties.rationale:
Anthony's explicit approval of a shape that was offered as a CORRECTION to his own proposal, which is worth recording as the sequence rather than just the outcome: he asked for graph-id enumeration, the enumeration was measured and found to answer a different question, the inverse was offered, and he took it. Checking the ask before building it is what made the difference, and it took one grep.

Recorded as accepted while `req:a-session-chooses-its-design` stays proposed. That is deliberate: he approved a MECHANISM, and the requirement's wording — particularly its second half about being pointed at a design — has not been read back to him. Promoting the requirement on the strength of approval for one half of it would be exactly the signature-forging `dec:certainty-derived` forbids.

The locking constraint is on the node rather than left for the build because a describe-tool that reports "no design" when the store is merely busy would reproduce `dec:no-design-here-never-looked` in a new place, and that is a cheap mistake to make.
